LH-REG-002.question: An insurer incorporated in Bermuda wants to sell life insurance policies to residents of Georgia. In Georgia, this company is classified as:
LH-REG-002.explanation: O.C.G.A. 33-3-1 defines an alien insurer as one formed under the laws of a country other than the United States. A foreign insurer is formed in another U.S. state, which is the tempting choice but applies only to companies formed within the United States.

LH-REG-003.question: An insurer incorporated in Ohio has received a certificate of authority from Georgia and sells policies there. In Georgia, it is considered:
LH-REG-003.explanation: Under O.C.G.A. 33-3-1 an insurer formed under the laws of another state is foreign, and one holding a Georgia certificate of authority is admitted (authorized) to transact business there. Non-admitted would apply only without a certificate, and it is domestic only in Ohio.

LH-PROV-004.explanation: Georgia requires every life policy to give a grace period of at least 30 days for each premium after the first, during which the policy stays in force (O.C.G.A. 33-25-3(a)(1)). Because death occurred within the grace period, the insurer pays the face amount minus the overdue premium: $100,000 - $1,200 = $98,800.

LH-PROV-005.explanation: Georgia requires life policies to allow reinstatement within three years of premium default, on evidence of insurability and payment of overdue premiums and any policy debt with interest (O.C.G.A. 33-25-3(a)(8)). Paying only the missed premium is not enough, and a policy surrendered for cash cannot be reinstated.

LH-HPRV-001.explanation: Georgia's required grace period provision is at least 10 days for monthly premiums, so coverage continues through June 11 and any unpaid premium can be deducted from a claim (O.C.G.A. 33-29-3(b)(3)). The 7-day minimum applies only to weekly premiums, and 30 days applies to other modes.

LH-HPRV-004.explanation: Georgia's time of payment of claims provision requires loss-of-time benefits to be paid at least at the end of each 30-day period while the disability continues, with any balance paid on receipt of final proof (O.C.G.A. 33-29-3(b)(8)). A lump sum would defeat the purpose of replacing ongoing income.

LH-GEN-017.explanation: Estoppel prevents a party from reasserting a right after its own conduct led the other party to rely on it giving that right up. By accepting late premiums for two years, the insurer led the owner to rely on that practice, so a court bars the lapse. Indemnity is the principle of restoring an insured to the pre-loss condition and has nothing to do with this dispute.

LH-LIFE-001.explanation: Under O.C.G.A. 33-24-3(h), an insurable interest must exist when a personal insurance contract becomes effective but need not exist when the loss occurs, so the divorce does not void Maria's policy. Denying the claim for lack of insurable interest at death is wrong.

excluded.LH-HPRV-003: Keys the NAIC claim-forms deadline of 15 days; Georgia's required provision gives the insurer 10 working days to furnish claim forms (O.C.G.A. 33-29-3(b)(6)), so the key is wrong for Georgia.
excluded.LH-TYPE-016: Keys 'life license plus FINRA registration' for variable life; Georgia also requires a separate Variable Products agent license (exam 62, handbook #121100), so the key is incomplete in Georgia.
excluded.LH-ANN-004: Same issue as LH-TYPE-016 for variable annuities (Georgia Variable Products line).
